title: VEAT Quantifies Implicit Associations in Text-to-Video Generator Sora and Reveals Challenges in Bias Mitigation

bias_targets.methodology: Applying the Video Embedding Association Test (VEAT) and Single-Category VEAT (SC-VEAT) to compute cosine similarities and Cohen's d effect sizes between CLIP embeddings of Sora-generated videos (prompted for European American vs. African American subjects/names) and attributes like valence (pleasant/unpleasant), occupations, and academic awards. Results are also correlated with real-world demographic statistics.

Using VEAT and SC-VEAT to measure associations by comparing CLIP embeddings of AI-generated videos (prompted for male vs. female subjects/terms) against video embeddings representing valence, 17 occupations, and 7 prestigious awards. The measured effect sizes are then correlated with real-world labor and laureate demographics.
